project.name: Apollo
project.description: Apollo is a reliable, centralized configuration management system designed for microservice architectures. It enables teams to manage configurations across different applications, environments, and clusters from a single unified interface. The system supports real-time configuration updates (hot release), version management, grayscale releases, and provides comprehensive authorization and audit capabilities. Apollo consists of a Spring Boot/Spring Cloud-based server and multiple client SDKs (Java and .Net) that operate independently of application frameworks.
project.architecture_summary: Apollo follows a multi-tier, microservice-oriented architecture. The server-side (Admin Service) is built on Spring Boot and Spring Cloud with a Spring Security-based authentication layer. The system is organized around domain modules including: (1) Configuration Management (apps, namespaces, clusters, configuration items, releases); (2) Gray Release Management (branch strategy, release rules); (3) Service Discovery & Registry (database-backed service discovery with caching); (4) Audit Logging (distributed tracing, operation tracking, data influence recording); (5) Message Distribution (database-driven release message propagation). The codebase uses JPA for persistence, RESTful controllers for API exposure, aspect-oriented programming for cross-cutting concerns (locking, audit tracing), and repository patterns for data access. Core business logic is coordinated through service classes that manage entity lifecycles and enforce business rules.
